read_from.rule: «no reply has landed» is a statement about THIS file, and the pod writes to its own. Copy the partial jsonl back BEFORE every gate: a KILL read off a file nobody refreshed would kill a healthy run and put the wrong reason in this record

boot_kill.rule: min(boot_kill_seconds, usable_seconds − seconds already elapsed since `pod create` − reading_projection_seconds). The contract's twelve minutes is a CEILING; what binds is whichever of the two comes first, because a boot that runs past the point where the remaining 23 threads no longer fit is spending on a pass that must stop anyway. Both numbers are printed at the gate and both land in the run record

The contract's twelve minutes is a CEILING; what binds is whichever of the two comes first, because a boot that runs past the point where the remaining 23 threads no longer fit is spending on a pass that must stop anyway. deadlines_at_open.which_binds: affordability — the generation has not started, so the contract's twelve minutes has no place on this axis yet

go_no_go.the_verdict_re_derives_from_here: `measured_seconds_per_thread` ≤ `seconds_per_thread_that_still_fits` IS the verdict. The dollars below are the same statement rounded, and at the margin both sides of it print the same figure
